title: Finding Areas with Integration
page_title: Finding Areas with Integration | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Additional Maths Revision Notes 2023

blocks.text: What does area under a curve mean?

blocks.md:
- The phrase “area under a curve” refers to the area bounded by …

  - ... the **x**-axis
  - … the graph of **y = f(x)**
  - … the vertical line **x = a**
  - … the vertical line **x = b**

blocks.alt: Example of area under a curve

blocks.text: How do I find the area under a curve?

blocks.md: - The value from **definite** **integration** is equal to the “area under a curve” ![Definite integration gives the area under a curve](assets/aa66133f4a6a-8-1-4-notes-fig2.png) ![Example of finding the area under a curve](assets/334f1688ae7c-8-1-4-notes-fig3.png)

blocks.text: What if I am not told the limits?

blocks.md:
- If limits are not provided they will likely be the **x**-axis intercepts

  - Set **y = 0** and solve the equation to find the **x**-axis intercepts

blocks.alt: Example of finding the limits of integration

blocks.text: What happens if the graph is below the x-axis?

blocks.md:
- If the area lies underneath the **x**-axis the value of the integral will be negative
- An **area** cannot be negative, so take the **modulus** of the integral ![Example of the area being below the x-axis](assets/d6a88b835609-8-1-4-notes-fig6.png)

blocks.alt: Another example of the area being below the x-axis

blocks.text: What if the area is made up of more than one section?

blocks.md:
- Be careful when one section is above and one section is below the **x**-axis

  - You will need a separate integral for each section, BUT...
  - ...One section's integral will be **negative**
  - ...One section's integral will be **positive**
  - So you’ll need to take the **modulus** before adding to find the total area

blocks.alt: Splitting the area into two areas

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Add information to any diagram provided in the question, as well as axes intercepts and values of limits
- Mark and shade the area you’re trying to find, and if no diagram is provided, **sketch** one!
